text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Anti-Corruption Agency has produced a "Top 10" list of government agencies and departments investigated for corrupt practices based on a 1990-1994 survey it conducted.

-- Defending her allegations that police refused to entertain cases of domestic violence, National Unity and Social Development Minister Zaleha Ismail went one step further and identified three police stations whose personnel refused to accept such reports.

-- The Cabinet, concerned over the rising trend in social ills plaguing the country, has set up a committee headed by Education Minister Najib Razak to carry out a comprehensive review of laws relating to social issues in an attempt to curb the problem.

-- Civil servants who resign to join privatised government agencies or professionals who leave to work in specialised areas can now rejoin the government service with no loss in seniority and other benefits.
-- The first six months of this year saw a total of 36 new companies listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, raising total gross proceeds of 2.719 billion ringgit.
-- The focus of the 1998 Budget Dialogue, which starts today, is to seek qualitative measures in ensuring higher economic growth which is supported by stronger productivity output.
-- Soon-to-be listed KUB Malaysia Bhd hopes to clinch privatisation deals overseas which it said will be undertaken together with a few other Malaysian and foreign companies.
